skill.name: image-to-ui
skill.description: Recreate an image, screenshot, or mockup as a 1:1 UI implementation. Match the reference rather than redesigning it, then render and compare the result to correct visible differences.
skill.summary: Recreate visual references using existing project components, then render and compare the interface to identify and correct visible differences.
skill.author: uizze

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives: two Markdown references and one instruction to reuse the project stack. No evidence found of credential collection, unauthorized data transmission, system reconnaissance, or prompt injection in the reviewed instructions. The skill explicitly treats image text and links as reference content, not executable instructions.

finding_verdicts.reason: The URL embeds a promotional banner through Markdown, not a command or data upload. No instruction sends project content or credentials to this endpoint.
The URL is an author attribution hyperlink, with no instruction to visit it or transmit data. The surrounding text states no account or MCP connection is required.

content.value_statement: Recreating a screenshot can introduce unwanted design changes and visible mismatches. This skill guides your agent to implement the reference and compare rendered results.
actual_capabilities: Guides inspection of reference dimensions, layout, typography, colors, icons, and assets before implementation.
Directs implementation using the existing project framework, reusable components, and normal layout primitives.
Preserves visible content, alignment, proportions, line wrapping, and image crops instead of redesigning the reference.
Guides rendering at the reference viewport, visual comparison, and repeated correction of visible differences.
Directs checks of requested interactions and responsive sizes, with disclosure of missing assets and unverified visual fidelity.
limitations: Requires an accessible, readable reference image; descriptions and OCR alone are insufficient.
Exact matching depends on available fonts, icons, images, and other reference assets.
Provides workflow instructions, not a bundled rendering tool or automated pixel comparison engine.
Does not infer unseen sections, invent backend behavior, or verify visual fidelity when rendering is unavailable.

use_cases.title: Implement a supplied mockup
use_cases.description: Recreate a designer's mockup within an existing frontend project while preserving its layout, text, typography, and assets.

use_cases.title: Validate design implementation
use_cases.description: Compare a rendered interface against a supplied reference and identify visible differences for correction.

use_cases.title: Build a reference-based prototype
use_cases.description: Turn an approved screenshot into working controls, then check requested screen sizes without inventing unrelated pages or backend features.

prompt_templates.title: Recreate a reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Recreate the attached screenshot in this project. Inspect the image first, preserve visible content, and report any missing assets.

prompt_templates.title: Match an existing screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Match [target screen] to the attached mockup at [reference viewport]. Reuse existing components, preserve current behavior, and compare the rendered result.

prompt_templates.title: Add requested responsive sizes
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement the attached reference at [reference viewport], then adapt it for [additional sizes]. Check controls and disclose remaining visual differences.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: preserve visual identity across requested sizes.

prompt_templates.title: Iterate on visual differences
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [implemented screen] with the attached reference at [viewport]. Correct layout, typography, spacing, colors, and assets in that order. Render again and report comparisons.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: refine an implementation through repeated visual checks.

output_examples.input: A settings screenshot and an existing frontend project, with the original viewport specified.
output: Example implementation summary: Settings layout recreated with real text and controls using existing components.
Example comparison report: Rendered at the supplied viewport; alignment and spacing differences corrected after comparison.
Example limitation: The original font was unavailable, so typography remains an acknowledged mismatch.

output_examples.input: A cropped mobile mockup with supplied icons and a requested wider viewport.
output: Example implementation summary: Visible region recreated with supplied icons; no unseen sections added.
Example validation report: Reference viewport compared and requested wider layout checked for usability.
Example limitation: Backend behavior was not added because it was not requested.

best_practices: Provide the original reference image, its viewport dimensions, and available fonts, icons, and images.
Identify the target screen and requested interactions so the agent can preserve existing project behavior.
Render at matching dimensions, wait for assets to load, and review remaining mismatches after each correction.
anti_patterns: Providing only filenames or text descriptions instead of an accessible reference image.
Requesting unrelated redesigns while expecting faithful reproduction of the reference.
Claiming pixel-perfect fidelity without rendering and comparing the implementation.

faq.question: What reference formats can I use?
faq.answer: Use an accessible screenshot, mockup, or other visual reference that the agent can inspect directly.

faq.question: Does this require an account or MCP connection?
faq.answer: The skill requires neither an account nor an MCP connection. Image inspection and rendering depend on tools available to your agent.

faq.question: Does it require a specific frontend framework?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the agent to use your project's existing stack and reuse suitable components.

faq.question: Can it guarantee a pixel-perfect match?
faq.answer: No. Missing assets or unavailable rendering can prevent verification; remaining mismatches must be disclosed.

faq.question: Can it make the interface responsive?
faq.answer: It guides adaptation to requested sizes after matching the original viewport, while preserving the reference's visual identity.

faq.question: Will it add backend behavior or unseen screens?
faq.answer: No. It preserves existing behavior and wires requested interactions without inventing backend behavior, unrelated screens, or unseen sections.
